builds.evidence: Relay-authorized movement (.nexus/approved_task.json SESSION_START, content-hash-verified; project/backlog.json id orchestrator_background_task_exit_race). Confirmed pre-fix state per the SESSION_START's own AC-2: ENGINEER_PROMPT did not instruct foreground/awaited validation regardless of the CLI's auto-background timeout, and decide_start had no detection for the dead-pid-plus-staged-changes pattern. Investigated the installed claude CLI (v2.1.263)'s own shipped behavior directly (its code reads BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, default 120000ms -- exactly the incident's '120s timeout' -- as the fallback for a Bash-tool call without its own explicit timeout, and BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, floored at that default, as the ceiling on an explicit one): a real lever exists, so scripts/orchestrator.py::_spawn_engineer now sets BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=1_800_000 (30 min) in the engineer's own env via setdefault (never overrides an operator's own value), raising both the fallback and the ceiling -- this does not disable auto-backgrounding outright (no such switch was found), so ENGINEER_PROMPT's own instruction is what the guarantee actually rests on, stated as such rather than overclaimed. Added pure functions relay_never_advanced_past_session_start / has_staged_uncommitted_changes / needs_resume_recovery_note (git status parsed/monkeypatched, no real subprocess spawn in the pure functions themselves) and wired them into _cmd_start's resume branch via a new _git_status_porcelain helper and _spawn_engineer's new extra_prompt_note parameter, which appends RESUME_RECOVERY_NOTE onto the prompt for exactly that one dispatch. No change to dispatch/refuse/ordinary-resume decisions, the merge-lock hook, or the privacy-gate hook. New tests in tests/test_orchestrator.py (pure-function coverage plus CLI-level resume-with-note/without-note integration tests); targeted run: 98 passed. Full one-shot regression (per DEV.TEST.1, run against the shared .venv next to the main checkout since this worktree has none of its own): 2963 passed, 25 skipped, 2 failed -- both pre-existing and unrelated (tests/test_dev_0_5b_auth_consumer_canonical_config.py's repository-text scan flags project/build_history.json's own prior entry for op0b_s7_s6_test_order_isolation, whose evidence text discusses this exact same class of false positive by naming, in prose, the two credential-shaped keyword/separator/quote patterns this repository's own DLP scanner treats as an assignment literal; confirmed by inspection that neither scripts/orchestrator.py nor tests/test_orchestrator.py appears anywhere in the failure list). git diff --check clean.

builds.title: OP.0b S7/S6 test-order isolation -- fix the module-rebind state leak
builds.summary: tests/test_op0b_s7_readiness_v2.py::test_evaluator_performs_no_socket_io_and_imports_no_collector popped checkpoint.preflight_collector / panorama.preflight_collector out of sys.modules without restoring them, so any later `import panorama.preflight_collector as pc` (S6's collector tests) rebound to a fresh module object while S6's already-imported collect_member kept resolving api_post/get_direct_system_info/get_firewall_api_key against the original module dict, silently defeating S6's own patches and issuing real HTTP calls when S7 ran first. Fixed at the source with a save/restore try/finally around the same test; added a direct regression test proving the restoration (mirroring the frontend-rendering shared-state-leak guard precedent). Test-infrastructure only, no product code changed. In passing, also fixed (PO-authorized, relay/NXS-LOCAL-0016 seq 2-3, "authorize narrow interpreter-resolution fix to the merge-lock re-validation hook"): scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py's merge-lock re-validation subprocess calls used sys.executable directly, which resolved to a pytest-less system python3 in this session (a worktree checkout has no .venv of its own -- every worktree shares the one .venv next to the main checkout). New _resolve_interpreter()/_validation_commands() locate the shared .venv via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (stable across every worktree), falling back to sys.executable only if no .venv is found. Narrow, scoped to that one call site per the PO's authorization; nothing else in the hook touched.
builds.evidence: Relay .nexus/approved_task.json SESSION_START (op0b_s7_s6_test_order_isolation, project/backlog.json). AC-1 reproduced at HEAD before any change: `pytest tests/test_op0b_s7_readiness_v2.py tests/test_op0b_s6_pan_preflight_collector.py` (S7 first) produced real S6 failures via a real, hanging `requests` connection attempt to the test fixture's synthetic management-IP target (F markers observed live during the run), exactly as backlog.json described. AC-2 root-caused by inspection: the sole `sys.modules.pop("panorama.preflight_collector"/"checkpoint.preflight_collector", None)` in the repo is tests/test_op0b_s7_readiness_v2.py::test_evaluator_performs_no_socket_io_and_imports_no_collector (grep-verified as the only occurrence); it asserts both names are absent from sys.modules at the end by design but never restores them, so S6's later `import panorama.preflight_collector as pc` inside `_collect`/`run_pan_preflight` call sites rebinds `pc` to a new module object that S6's own `patch.object(pc, ...)` calls target, while `collect_member` (imported by S6's test file at collection time, before S7 executes) keeps resolving its api_post/get_direct_system_info/get_firewall_api_key globals against the ORIGINAL module dict -- a module-rebind/state-leak, same family as the frontend-rendering guard precedent (tests/test_frontend_rendering_boundary.py::test_render_uitest_restores_the_builders_it_injects). AC-3 fix: the popped sys.modules entries are captured before the pop and restored in a try/finally wrapping the existing test body; no reordering, no renaming, no global conftest hack. AC-4 order-independence: both invocation orders green -- `pytest tests/test_op0b_s7_readiness_v2.py tests/test_op0b_s6_pan_preflight_collector.py` = 110 passed; reverse order = 110 passed; each file alone unchanged in count (S7 69 incl. 1 new regression test, S6 41) -- plus a new direct regression test, tests/test_op0b_s7_readiness_v2.py::test_evaluator_probe_restores_the_collector_modules_it_pops, that asserts checkpoint.preflight_collector / panorama.preflight_collector module identity is unchanged before/after the probing test runs, so a future regression of this class is caught locally rather than surfacing as 25 unrelated S6 failures. AC-5: no product code changed (test file only, confirmed via git diff). AC-6: both files green individually and in both orders; pass counts unchanged apart from the one deliberately added regression test; no test skipped or removed. Interpreter-resolution fix verified directly: gate._resolve_interpreter() now returns the shared .venv path even from a real `git worktree add` checkout with no .venv of its own (new tests/test_nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py::test_resolve_interpreter_finds_shared_venv_via_git_common_dir), and falls back to sys.executable when no .venv exists (test_resolve_interpreter_falls_back_to_sys_executable_without_a_venv). The interpreter-resolution fix is scoped to scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py's merge-lock re-validation call sites only, per the PO's own authorization (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0016 seq 3); it does not touch the hook's other sys.executable use (the merge-lock acquire/release orchestrator.py subprocess call), which was not reported broken and was left as-is.

builds.title: GOV.PO.3 -- resume canonical-relay access fix: --add-dir the canonical relay directory on every engineer spawn
builds.summary: Closes the finding recorded in relay/NXS-LOCAL-0012's SESSION_CLOSE (`next`): a resumed engineer session (`orchestrator start`'s `--resume` path) could not read/write the canonical relay file outside its own worktree, while a fresh dispatch could -- blocking every future interrupted/resumed movement from completing autonomously (GOV_PO_3_APPROVED_MOVEMENT_ORCHESTRATION.md section 3.7's own recovery design). Root cause (AC-2, confirmed live, not assumed): with `--permission-prompts none` a Read/Edit/Write-tool call to a path outside the worktree has no approval surface, is auto-denied, and stays denied for the rest of the session with no retries; a fresh dispatch only ever appeared to work because it happened to route relay access through Bash-invoked `scripts/local_relay.py`, which this per-tool directory allowlist does not gate -- nothing guaranteed a resumed session would route the same way. Fix (AC-3): `scripts/orchestrator.py::_spawn_engineer` now passes `--add-dir <canonical_relay_dir>` identically for a fresh dispatch and a resume, so access no longer depends on which tool a session happens to pick.
builds.evidence: Relay relay/NXS-LOCAL-0015-resume-canonical-relay-access-fix.json, validated protocol-v2 SESSION_START. AC-4 real reproduction (not a simplified proxy): dispatched a throwaway scratch movement (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0017-gov-po-3-resume-fix-ac4-repro-postfix.json, now CLOSED) through the real `scripts/orchestrator.py` -- fresh dispatch posted RELAY_ACK+RELAY_QUESTION and exited; a RELAY_DECISION was posted; a real orchestrator resume (no simplified proxy) re-read the canonical relay file fresh from disk and quoted the RELAY_DECISION's subject verbatim in its own RELAY_NOTE, reproducing and closing the exact gap found live in relay/NXS-LOCAL-0012. AC-5 (no regression): fresh-dispatch access was exercised in the same real run and still works, and tests/test_orchestrator.py::test_spawn_engineer_grants_add_dir_for_the_canonical_relay_directory_on_fresh_dispatch asserts the fresh-dispatch argv shape explicitly. New tests/test_orchestrator.py (+2): fresh-dispatch and resume both get the identical `--add-dir <canonical_relay_dir>` grant, resume argv ending in `--resume <session_id>` unchanged otherwise. This branch reconciled two concurrent merges to origin/main during integration: relay/NXS-LOCAL-0013 (gov_po_3_orchestrator_observability, PR #129 -- both movements changed `_spawn_engineer`'s argv construction, reconciled by hand so `--add-dir` and `--output-format stream-json --verbose` coexist, and this movement's two tests updated to read the engineer process's own Popen call now that a second, summary-tailer Popen call is also made) and relay/NXS-LOCAL-0010 (m10_3_entity_and_vendor_support_producers, PR #131 -- unrelated files, bookkeeping-only conflict). Full one-shot suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -n auto --dist worksteal` (post-merge): 2699 passed, 25 skipped, 2 failed -- both pre-existing/unrelated (tests/test_dev_0_5b_auth_consumer_canonical_config.py's own DLP-collision self-check against repository prose, same documented false positive as prior builds). git diff --check clean.
builds.risks_forward: In passing, this movement's engineer session found (documented, NOT fixed here -- out of scope per this movement's own invariant against other orchestrator.py behavior changes): `scripts/orchestrator.py` never persists the real `claude` session_id (always None), so its 'resume' path never actually passes `--resume` to the `claude` CLI; it currently works only because a fresh re-spawn into the same worktree/branch behaves equivalently for this task shape. A follow-up movement should fix session-id persistence itself.

builds.title: GOV.PO.3 -- orchestrator observability: streaming engineer output + watch dashboard
builds.summary: Extends the already-frozen scripts/orchestrator.py (docs/design/GOV_PO_3_APPROVED_MOVEMENT_ORCHESTRATION.md section 3.4) with real-time visibility: the engineer's claude -p invocation now streams stream-json output incrementally instead of only at process exit, a new dependency-free parser derives a human-readable engineer.summary.log alongside the raw log, orchestrator status gains a last_activity field, and a new read-only `orchestrator watch` terminal dashboard polls the same status data in a loop until Ctrl-C. Backward compatible with movements dispatched before this change.
builds.evidence: Relay relay/NXS-LOCAL-0013-orchestrator-observability.json, validated protocol-v2 SESSION_START (Product Owner direction immediately after AC-3/AC-5 demonstration 1 of gov_po_3_approved_movement_orchestration_ac3 ran live and confirmed engineer.log stayed empty until process exit under the prior, non-streaming claude -p invocation -- a real, observed gap). Verified the exact flag spelling for real before coding, per this movement's own requirement: `claude -p --help` against the installed claude 2.1.263, and a live `claude -p ... --output-format stream-json` run without --verbose, which fails closed with 'Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose' -- confirming both flags are required together, not assumed from documentation. _spawn_engineer's argv now carries --output-format stream-json --verbose alongside the existing -p; a second, detached `_tail-summary` subprocess (an internal, undocumented CLI subcommand, never invoked directly) tails engineer.log from a byte offset, decodes and summarizes each complete line with a new stdlib-only, dependency-free parser (summarize_stream_json_line), and appends one line per event to a sibling engineer.summary.log -- a truncated last line at read time is left unconsumed and re-read once complete, never dropped or crashed on; an unrecognized-but-valid JSON shape falls back to a truncated raw-JSON one-liner rather than being silently dropped, per this movement's own named risk. The parser's real-shape table (assistant text/tool_use/thinking, user tool_result ok/error, result, system, rate_limit_event) was captured from a real `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose` run against the installed claude version, not invented. Live end-to-end smoke test (outside the unit suite, since AC-6 explicitly excludes spawning a real terminal from the test suite itself): a background writer appended the same real line shapes to a growing log file while `_tail-summary` polled it at a 0.1s interval against the writer's own pid, producing the expected three-line engineer.summary.log incrementally, then performed its own final catch-up drain and exited cleanly once the writer pid died. orchestrator status gained last_activity (the most recent engineer.summary.log line, or null); the new `watch` subcommand polls the same _status_row data status already computes via a new read-only _gather_watch_rows (never calls _save_state), clears and redraws a stdlib-only (os.system/shutil.get_terminal_size) table -- movement id, phase, pid-alive, heartbeat age, branch, worktree, last relay marker+timestamp, last activity -- truncated to terminal width, and exits cleanly on Ctrl-C; its docstring states explicitly why it loops until interrupted rather than returning after one bounded wait like local_relay.py's own watch (a human-facing live dashboard vs. an unattended, hard-timeout-ceilinged polling primitive). Backward compatibility verified directly: a movement record whose worktree_path has no .nexus/engineer.summary.log at all (the pre-this-movement shape) produces last_activity=None / rendered 'n/a' in both status and watch, no exception. Validation: tests/test_orchestrator.py, 28 new (across 21 new test functions, one parametrized 8 ways over the real-shape table) plus the 48 pre-existing, 76 passed, 0 failed. Full one-shot suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -n auto --dist worksteal`: 2690 passed, 25 skipped, 2 failed -- both the same pre-existing, already-documented tests/test_dev_0_5b_auth_consumer_canonical_config.py DLP-scan false positive against this repository's own build_history.json/relay evidence text (gov_po_1_gate_5_worktree_management's and gov_po_1_local_relay_watch_command's own evidence already document the identical two failures), confirmed unrelated -- neither failing test nor the lines it flags were touched by this movement's diff. git diff --check clean. builds.title: GOV.PO.3 -- push-hook baseline scoping: block only genuinely new privacy findings
builds.summary: Fixes the live bug found during GOV.PO.3 AC-5 demonstration 1 (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0012 seq 3-4): scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py's pre-push privacy gate ran scan_repository() against the full working tree and failed closed on ANY finding, including pre-existing repository debt (two prose false positives in project/build_history.json and relay/NXS-LOCAL-0003-...json), blocking an unrelated one-file push and every orchestrated push thereafter. The hook is now baseline-aware: it scans the working tree, and only when that scan is non-empty also scans the movement's own recorded base commit (via `git archive` into a throwaway tempdir, reusing scan_repository() unmodified -- no new scanning code path) and blocks only findings absent from that baseline. Findings are matched on (path, rule, a sha256 fingerprint of the flagged line's stripped content), not (path, exact line number), so a pre-existing finding whose line shifted from unrelated earlier edits still counts as pre-existing. A denial names only the genuinely new finding(s).
builds.evidence: Relay relay/NXS-LOCAL-0014-push-hook-baseline-scoping.json, validated protocol-v2 SESSION_START, dispatched by scripts/orchestrator.py into this movement's own git worktree. Read scripts/nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py in full before editing, per the SESSION_START's own requirement. New tests/test_nexus_engineer_tool_gate.py (7 tests, all against a synthetic git-repo fixture except the last): pre-existing finding untouched by the diff (push allowed); pre-existing finding whose containing file the diff also touches elsewhere, flagged span unchanged (still allowed); pre-existing finding surviving line-number drift from unrelated earlier edits (still recognized as pre-existing); a genuinely new finding (push denied, message names only the new finding, not the pre-existing one alongside it); the zero-findings case skipping the baseline scan entirely (monkeypatched to assert it is never called); handle_pre wiring the check into an actual `git push` decision end to end; and a regression test reproducing the exact AC-1 live-bug findings (project/build_history.json's own CREDENTIAL_LITERAL match and relay/NXS-LOCAL-0003-local-relay-watch-command.json:155) against this repository's real current state, asserting both are recognized as pre-existing via the baseline scan. All 7 passed. tests/test_orchestrator.py unaffected: 48 passed. git diff --check clean. Repository privacy gate `.venv/bin/python main.py --repository-privacy-check` (the unmodified, out-of-scope CI/full-tree scan, run once per the validation plan): FAIL/5 findings -- confirmed via a direct gate._privacy_check() call that the two AC-1 findings are now recognized as pre-existing (not named in the denial); the remaining 3 (data/, data/.support_hmac.key, logs/) are untracked local runtime artifacts with no committed baseline to match against, a separate, already-documented, out-of-scope gap (same pattern as gov_po_1_gate_5's and gov_po_1_local_relay_watch_command's own evidence).
builds.risks_forward: The baseline scan resolves report.git.base via `git merge-base HEAD <base>` and exports that commit with `git archive`; a movement whose .nexus/approved_task.json is missing or whose base ref cannot be resolved locally degrades to treating the working-tree scan as authoritative with no baseline credit (documented as 'baseline unavailable' in the pass/deny reason) rather than failing the hook itself -- unchanged from today's behavior in that case, not a regression, but also not exercised by the synthetic fixtures here beyond the missing-approved-task path implicit in _approved_task_git_base's own None-returning branches.

builds.title: GOV_PO_1_GATE_5 -- allow git worktree add/list from interactive PO sessions

builds.evidence: Relay relay/NXS-LOCAL-0006-gate-5-worktree-management.json, validated protocol-v2 SESSION_START. Verified git worktree add's actual argument grammar via `git worktree add --help` before implementing: `git worktree add [-f] [--detach] [--checkout] [--lock [--reason <s>]] [--orphan] [(-b | -B) <new-branch>] <path> [<commit-ish>]` -- boolean flags carry no value, -b/-B and --reason each consume the following token, and whatever tokens remain in order are the positionals (path, then commit-ish). builds.title: GOV.PO.1 -- bounded, read-only `watch` subcommand for the local relay
builds.summary: Adds a bounded, read-only `watch` subcommand to scripts/local_relay.py so a session can wait for a relay file's next_actor to flip without manual re-checking (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0003-local-relay-watch-command.json's SESSION_START, Product Owner direction after real relay#11-#16/local-relay-protocol use surfaced this friction). Never a background daemon by construction (--timeout has a hard ceiling and --interval a hard floor), never writes to the file it watches, and never itself authorizes acting on a detected next_actor flip.
builds.evidence: Branch feature/gov-po-1-local-relay-watch-command from origin/main (c406a80). Read scripts/local_relay.py and docs/design/LOCAL_RELAY_PROTOCOL.md section 8 in full before implementing, per the SESSION_START's requirements. Added `watch --file FILE --for {po|engineer} [--interval SECONDS] [--timeout SECONDS]` to scripts/local_relay.py: default interval 20s (hard floor 5s, usage error below it), default timeout 1800s (hard ceiling 3600s, usage error above it), a new documented exit code 3 ('timeout, no change') alongside the existing 0/1/2 convention, strictly read-only (only _load_json_file calls; no write path). Checks next_actor immediately, then polls every --interval seconds up to the deadline; on a match, prints one JSON line {next_actor, entries} naming every entry with seq greater than the entry count observed at watch start, and exits 0; on timeout with no match, exits 3 with the file untouched. scripts/nexus_po_tool_gate.py: added the four local_relay.py watch interpreter-spelling prefixes to COMMON_PREFIXES (both PO forms, read-only, mirroring status/validate). docs/design/LOCAL_RELAY_PROTOCOL.md section 8 updated (not replaced) to document watch precisely: bounded, blocking, explicit-invocation-only, decides nothing -- RELAY_DECISION-class authorization is unchanged. New tests: tests/test_local_relay_protocol.py (+9: immediate match with zero sleeps, a simulated mid-poll flip via a real append call inside a monkeypatched time.sleep, timeout with a fake monotonic clock, the AC-3 byte-for-byte-unchanged-on-timeout proof, interval-floor and timeout-ceiling usage errors, missing-file and invalid-file handling); tests/test_gov_po_role.py (+1: watch allowlisted in both delegated and interactive forms, mirroring the existing status/validate test). Validation: targeted tests/test_local_relay_protocol.py + tests/test_gov_po_role.py, 168 passed; full regression `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -n auto --dist worksteal`, 2585 passed, 25 skipped, 2 failed -- both pre-existing and unrelated to this movement (tests/test_dev_0_5b_auth_consumer_canonical_config.py's repository-text scan walks .venv/ site-packages on this machine's checkout, since _repository_text_candidates() excludes only .git/__pycache__/.pytest_cache/node_modules, and third-party packages such as paramiko/httpcore contain literal 'password='/'PASSWORD:' substrings; confirmed unrelated by inspection -- neither that test nor the code it scans was touched by this movement). git diff --check clean. Repository privacy gate `.venv/bin/python main.py --repository-privacy-check`: FAIL/3 findings, all pre-existing local runtime artifacts outside git (data/, data/.support_hmac.key, logs/ -- all .gitignore'd, untracked, unrelated to this movement's changed files).
builds.risks_forward: None specific to watch's own behavior. This movement's SESSION_START scoped the doc change to docs/design/LOCAL_RELAY_PROTOCOL.md section 8 only; section 9's CLI synopsis and exit-code table still lists only create/append/status/validate -- a future movement should extend section 9 to keep the full CLI reference in sync. A caller can set a low --interval with the --timeout ceiling to approximate a near-continuous poll for up to an hour; this is a deliberate, documented consequence of the bound (section 8), not an oversight.

builds.title: GOV_PO_1_GATE_1 -- fix nexus_po_tool_gate.py false positives and enable packet emission
builds.summary: Corrects scripts/nexus_po_tool_gate.py, found blocking the first real Phase A PLAN episode (gov_po_1_step_5_first_plan): its naive substring ban on '<'/'>'/';'/'|' rejected any command containing those characters even inside quoted data, blocking a standard git commit trailer's <email> and leaving no way to post the SESSION_START/SESSION_CLOSE relay packets section 5.1.1 requires (Write access is limited to 8 governance paths; there was no route to stage packet content without either Write outside those paths or banned shell redirection/piping). Replaces the substring check with shlex(punctuation_chars=True) tokenization, which reproduces bash's actual distinction (a metacharacter embedded in a quoted argument stays data; the same character standalone is a real operator), keeps backtick/$( banned unconditionally since bash still executes those inside double quotes, converts the destructive-word bans (rm/mv/cp/sudo/chmod/curl/wget/ssh/main.py) from substrings to exact tokens (this also newly denies `find ... -exec rm ...`, which the substring form missed since 'rm' there is a genuine bare token), denies a raw embedded newline outright (bash's other statement separator), and adds one narrow, auditable scratch-write allowance (nexus_po_*.json/.txt directly under a recognized system temp root, interactive form only) plus a matching restriction that --body-file may reference only that scratch pattern (closing an exfiltration path the prior test suite had accidentally asserted as allowed for an arbitrary filename). Also neutralizes an unrelated, real exposure found in the same review: the untracked .claude/settings.local.json on this workstation carried a blanket Bash(gh pr merge:*) allow rule that -- per section 6.2 item I3 -- would have applied uncontested to a PO session launched from the VS Code extension without --settings .claude/nexus-po.settings.json (the extension cannot pass that flag); emptied to permissions.allow: [] directly on the workstation, not part of this PR (untracked, gitignored, not repository state).
builds.evidence: Isolated fix branch gov-po-1-gate-fix via git worktree from origin/main a7fca51 (deliberately NOT switching branches in the primary working directory, which the live gov_po_1_step_5_first_plan PO episode was actively using at 0fa39e2 / PR #113). Verified real bash semantics before implementing: quoted <email> stays one token under shlex(punctuation_chars=True); unquoted a>b and a > b both yield a standalone '>' token; find ... -exec rm -rf {} \; tokenizes 'rm' as its own bare word. Verified the actual macOS discrepancy between tempfile.gettempdir() (a per-user $TMPDIR path) and the conventional /tmp (a symlink to /private/tmp) that the first test run surfaced, and widened the scratch-root recognition to accept both, realpath-resolved. Proved the exact end-to-end flow section 5.1.1 requires now passes the gate: Write a scratch input JSON, render it with the unmodified, still-FROZEN scripts/gov_session_transfer.py, post it via gh issue create --body-file referencing only that scratch output. Validation: tests/test_gov_po_role.py (57, incl. 9 new: git-commit-trailer allowed, quoted operators not falsely flagged, real chaining/redirection/dangerous-bare-words/find-exec/newline/malformed-quoting all still denied, scratch write allowed for interactive only with traversal rejected, --body-file restricted to the scratch pattern, and the full render-then-post sequence) + relay + session-transfer + convergence: 209 passed; repository privacy gate PASS; git diff --check clean.

The scratch pattern is deliberately narrow (nexus_po_*.json/.txt under a recognized temp root); a future need for a different staging shape should extend the same regex, not add a second mechanism. This movement is independent of and does not touch gov_po_1_step_5_first_plan (PR #113, branch gov/po-1-step-5-first-plan) or M10.1; that PLAN episode's own SESSION_START/SESSION_CLOSE packet posting is unblocked by this fix but was not itself re-run here.

builds.title: M4 -- Local control-plane metadata store (approved Option A)
builds.summary: Added the additive local SQLite control-plane metadata store under RuntimeRoot data_root, owning only job definitions, job/run lifecycle records, schedules, capability projections, idempotency/submission metadata and control-plane runtime metadata. Storage infrastructure only: no job behaviour, target resolution, runner, scheduler, enrollment, HTTP/UI surface or device contact, and the PCP.1 Device Registry stays filesystem JSON and unmigrated.
builds.evidence: Schema version 1, seven tables (schema_migrations, control_plane_metadata, job_definitions, job_submissions, job_runs, schedules, capability_projections), all STRICT. SQLite runtime: journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=FULL (chosen over WAL's usual NORMAL because CON.0 section 7.9 requires a job record durable before the runner may start it, and NORMAL can lose a committed record on power loss), foreign_keys=ON, explicit busy_timeout=5000ms, all read back from the engine rather than assumed. Migrations are explicit, monotonic and one-transaction-per-version; a failure rolls its own version back and leaves earlier versions applied. Fail-closed typed outcomes for invalid placement, unsupported/newer schema (naming encountered and supported versions), corruption or non-database content, failed migration, bounded contention timeout and uniqueness/foreign-key violation; corrupt files are left byte-for-byte untouched, never repaired, recreated, downgraded or discarded. Uniqueness: idempotency_key is the job_submissions primary key, and a partial unique index enforces at most one active run per durable job definition. Ownership boundary proven against the real schema -- a test walks every column of every table and fails on any endpoint/address/credential/secret/token/trust/raw-config/backup/CAS fragment; targets are stored only as opaque device_id or logical_entity_id references, never a copied endpoint. Capability projections persist only D2-D6 dimension values, basis/run information, semantic identity and producer/support-rule context plus every consumed authority generation (AC-CS-71) and an identity_mapping_proven flag (AC-CS-97); primary_status, qualifiers, evidence presentation, shell composition, affordances, action declarations, taxonomy and authorization state have no column and are test-enforced absent. Privacy extended, not duplicated: the store lives at data_root/state/control_plane.db, outside the data/runs/* subtree run_support_bundle enumerates, so bundle exclusion is structural and support_bundle.py was not modified; .db/.db-wal/.db-shm were already DATABASE_ARTIFACT in the privacy gate and already gitignored, and the store is now registered LOCAL-SENSITIVE (CLASS 2) in PRIVACY_AND_DATA_HANDLING.md. Added a ninth evidence_backend concern selector that refuses postgres explicitly, naming pcp_storage_engine as still open -- SQLite is not the production engine (AC-ST-7). Validation: 57 focused tests in tests/test_m4_control_plane_metadata_store.py plus 161 passed / 9 skipped across architecture, privacy-gate, PCP.1 registry, support-bundle, CON.2 console-job, evidence-backend and runtime-paths suites. Automated tests do not prove production readiness or real-environment validation; no device was contacted. PO correction round (one bounded round, same branch): the migration ledger is now validated as an EXACT PREFIX of MIGRATIONS rather than by max(version) alone -- a ledger carrying the supported version under a foreign migration name, an unknown lower or extra version, a gap, a non-prefix sequence, or an unreadable foreign column set is refused with the typed schema-version outcome naming the encountered ledger and highest version and the supported ledger and version range. Duplicate and out-of-order entries are structurally impossible in this build's own ledger (version is an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, so rowid is the version) and are refused where they are representable, in a foreign unkeyed ledger table; both shapes are tested. Open order was corrected so every refusal precedes every persistent mutation: connection-local busy_timeout/foreign_keys, then the corruption probe, then ledger validation, and only then WAL activation, synchronous=FULL, ledger creation and pending migrations -- so a refused database keeps its journal mode, its ledger and its table set and grows no -wal/-shm sidecars. Connection cleanup is deterministic: _connect closes its own handle if configuration fails and the open sequence closes on BaseException, proven by tracking every connection the module creates across configuration-failure, corruption and ledger refusals. Focused tests 57 -> 74.

builds.title: DEV.TEST.1 -- Parallelize local and GitHub Actions full-regression execution
builds.summary: Replaced the GitHub Actions full-regression job's serial `python -m pytest -q` (measured 11m56s, workflow run 34016204567) with `python -m pytest -q -n auto --dist worksteal`, proven green on a real push-to-main run (workflow run 34020356372): 4 workers, 1944 passed / 38 skipped / 0 failed in 275.74s (4m35.74s). Final Product Owner-directed CI topology (same-session correction): `pull_request` schedules `validate` only, `full-regression` runs exclusively via explicit `workflow_dispatch` -- no automatic trigger on pull_request or push to main, and the workflow's `push:` trigger is removed entirely (it would otherwise produce an empty, zero-job run). Pure test-execution infrastructure, no product behavior change, M3 not started.
builds.evidence: PHASE 1 AUDIT: inventoried every full-suite invocation (this workflow's two jobs, scripts/pytest_one_shot.ps1, requirements-dev.txt, docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md, AI_START_HERE.md, CLAUDE.md) before changing anything. ROOT CAUSE: the full-regression job's own long-standing 'serial on purpose' comment traced to one concrete defect -- scripts/render_uitest.py::render() left three utils.html_export payload builders bare-rebound (not monkeypatch.setattr) after use, so the rebind silently outlived the call and leaked into whichever later in-process run_html_export() shared its worker/process; that is already fixed with a try/finally restore (scripts/render_uitest.py::_injected_builders) and directly regression-tested regardless of worker/ordering (tests/test_frontend_rendering_boundary.py::test_render_uitest_restores_the_builders_it_injects). No other shared-mutable-resource pattern (fixed ports beyond OS-assigned port 0, os.chdir, module-global caches, tracked-file mutation) was found across tests/ -- no serial exception group required. TOPOLOGY: Candidate A, one pytest-xdist process (`-n auto --dist worksteal`), selected over a fixed worker count (Candidate B, no evidence the runner's CPU count needs pinning over `-n auto`) or matrix sharding (Candidate C, unneeded shard-membership/aggregation/browser-provisioning complexity) or a hybrid with a serial exception set (Candidate D, no test requires one) -- the smallest design that already matched the command proven locally and in scripts/pytest_one_shot.ps1/requirements-dev.txt. LOCAL VALIDATION (accepted by Product Owner as pre-merge evidence in place of a PR-triggered cloud run, since no PR-triggered run was available -- see incident below): two clean `python3 -m pytest -q -n auto --dist worksteal` runs (4 CPUs) -- 1957 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed at 32.27s and 35.01s, 1981 collected both times. PR #87 opened, evaluated a pull_request-trigger expansion (removing full-regression's `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` guard) to get automatic pre-merge cloud proof, then reverted it per Product Owner direction back to the original approved policy (pull_request = fast validate only; push-to-main/workflow_dispatch = parallel full-regression) -- a standalone decision independent of the incident below. PR #87 merged (081a976a3e1cc16fb57af7f0c9aa0e0501a7625b's successor chain -> 06f73e7df7f80cf415fd146356a677b71e6522b7). POST-MERGE YAML-SYNTAX INCIDENT (corrects an in-session misdiagnosis): every CI trigger (push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch) on every branch, including the push-to-main run for the PR #87 merge commit itself, completed with a zero-job failing check suite. This was FIRST MISDIAGNOSED as an environment/automation-identity limitation preventing GitHub Actions from scheduling pull_request/workflow_dispatch jobs on a non-default branch (based on a genuine but coincidental `workflow_dispatch` 403 from this session's own token permissions, and a pattern-match against zero-job check suites that looked identity-correlated). THAT DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. Parsing .github/workflows/validation.yml locally after merge found the real cause: the 'Report worker topology' step's `run:` value was an unquoted plain YAML scalar containing a bare `: ` inside an f-string label ("...target): {os.cpu_count()}"), which YAML parses as an illegal nested mapping -- a file that fails to parse cannot schedule a job under any trigger, on any branch, regardless of who pushed it, exactly the symptom observed. Fixed via PR #88 (rewording the f-string) and merged (211aafb5eddf8d6a5e0ba6b996decc190450141f -> 6ca67cce2c25a8a29f0e1207c5851d0e2756f7f9); every place this session's own docs/state had stated the wrong theory as fact was corrected to describe the real cause. New permanent guard: tests/test_ci_workflow_fast_pr_regression.py::test_workflow_yaml_parses (pyyaml>=6 added to requirements-dev.txt) actually parses the workflow file on every test run so this exact defect class fails locally before a future push. REAL GITHUB ACTIONS CLOUD PROOF (the actual point of this movement): push-to-main run https://github.com/ozandurmus/neXus/actions/runs/34020356372 (event push, commit 6ca67cce2c25a8a29f0e1207c5851d0e2756f7f9, triggered automatically by the PR #88 merge, job full-regression) -- conclusion SUCCESS. Job log (fetched directly via the GitHub API, not inferred from YAML text): 'CPU count (xdist -n auto target) -> 4'; `python -m pytest -q -n auto --dist worksteal`; 'bringing up nodes...' (xdist controller); final summary '1944 passed, 38 skipped, 3 warnings in 275.74s (0:04:35)' -- 1982 collected (differs from the local 1981 by one test, an environment-dependent collection difference between this sandbox and the GitHub-hosted runner, e.g. Playwright/paramiko/postgres availability -- not a coverage gap: 0 failed either way). Full test suite step wall-clock (start-to-finish, from the job's own step timestamps): 07:53:55Z-07:58:31Z = 4m36s; pytest's own reported time 275.74s (4m35.74s) matches. Overall job (full-regression) duration 07:53:39Z-07:58:33Z ~= 4m54s; validate job correctly SKIPPED (push event, not pull_request). Whitespace/conflict-marker check step exited 2 (pre-existing repo-wide findings in files this movement never touched -- configuration/panorama_config_collector.py, several docs/history/phase/*.md, several static/*.js, utils/diff.py -- identical to every prior run's known findings) but is `continue-on-error: true` by design, so it did not affect the job's SUCCESS conclusion. builds.title: OP.0b S8-P0.1 - CP SSH strict trust-store preflight correction
builds.summary: Correction prerequisite discovered while preparing S8-A: the shared 0.6.4 strict host-key helper (utils/cp_ssh_trust.py) loaded trusted keys into Paramiko's read-only system store (load_system_host_keys) but gated on the separate writable local store (get_host_keys), so strict=True was unusable even with a correctly provisioned system/user known_hosts; the strict precondition now means 'at least one configured trusted host-key source was successfully loaded', derived through public Paramiko APIs only (explicit system known_hosts path + paramiko.HostKeys parse of the same file), with unreadable/malformed sources failing closed under distinct value-free reason tokens. builds.title: CP remote collection - DONE-marker-loss diagnostic hardening
builds.summary: A real run hit RuntimeError('CP remote collection ended without DONE marker') with exit_status=0. First pass (this build's original commit) aligned checkpoint/cp_runner.py's _run_remote_collection channel-drain loop with checkpoint/direct_ssh_probe.py's tight-drain idiom and added safe diagnostic fields (exit_status/processed_gw/total_gw/stderr_bytes/last_marker) -- did not resolve the recurrence, but the new fields (processed_gw=0, total_gw=None, last_marker=None, stderr_bytes=658) proved the channel-drain race was NOT the cause and located the failure to before checkpoint/scripts/cp_inventory.sh line ~94 (TOTAL_GW is never even echoed), with real stderr output the code was discarding. Second pass: captures a bounded (8192-char) in-memory stderr sample and classifies it into safe, non-identity-bearing category tokens (no_such_file_or_directory, command_not_found, permission_denied, not_a_tty, unbound_variable, syntax_error, connection_reset_or_broken_pipe, or unclassified) via _classify_stderr_sample() -- the raw sample is discarded immediately after classification, never logged or raised (AGENTS.md raw-evidence law). Both the DONE-marker-missing and nonzero-exit-status RuntimeErrors now report stderr_classification alongside stderr_bytes. Root cause remains UNKNOWN -- still not a confirmed fix -- but the next real run will report which category of error is actually occurring instead of only a byte count.

builds.title: VSX real-env retry - three post-merge defects found and fixed
builds.summary: Real-environment retry of the VSX operational-identity correction (PR #30) against a live physical VSX pair found three defects invisible to synthetic unit tests: (1) checkpoint/scripts/cp_inventory.sh's echo|tr SAFE_GW pipeline silently appended a trailing underscore to every collected CP device name (echo's own newline being converted by tr, not a real naming convention), which propagated into (2) VSX-vs-ClusterXL misclassification and VS Virtual Systems splitting into per-member duplicates instead of merging under one cluster parent, and (3) HA-runtime checks always reporting INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE because two independently-computed entity-id strings for the same device diverged by that artifact. Fixed at the source (SAFE_GW strip) plus defensive join-key normalization in utils/failover/assessment.py; also threaded the VSX vsys context name into each Virtual System unit's display_name and widened the zero-padded member-ordinal display-name regex.
builds.evidence: tests/test_op0a_ha_readiness.py grew 2 tests reproducing the exact real-env device-name-separator and cp_ha_runtime entity-id shapes reported against the real pair. tests/test_phase0_5_3_cluster_hierarchy_ui.py grew 1 test for zero-padded member ordinals. tests/test_phase0_4_2_parallel_cp.py grew 1 test reproducing the echo/tr SAFE_GW pipeline bug directly. Full suite 1074 passed / 26 skipped / 0 failed. Confirmed against the real FW-CKP-EXTRA-LL and FW-CKP-ARKTEST pairs by the product owner after each fix.
builds.risks_forward: Fix applies only to collections run after this change -- output/cp.json etc. captured before it still carry the trailing-underscore artifact until re-collected. The defensive join-key normalization in assessment.py stays in place as a safety net for that stale data and any other, not-yet-seen instance of the same separator quirk.

builds.title: Operator Console -- CON.2 job engine and read-class actions
builds.summary: Implemented docs/history/phase/CON_2_CONSOLE_JOB_ENGINE_READ_ACTIONS.md against the frozen contract, after C-D3 (Provenance.CONSOLE vs reusing 'manual') was put to the product owner and resolved to add 'console' per the on-file recommendation. utils/collection_executor.py gained workflow_argv() (C2-2), promoted out of application/workflows/maintenance.py's _scheduler_workflow_argv, which is now a one-line wrapper over it -- the scheduler and the console job runner share one argv construction path. utils/coordinator_backend.py gained Provenance.CONSOLE = 'console' (C2-3); the required consumer audit found every consumer (Job.to_manifest_dict, RunContext.set_job_metadata, both InMemory/Postgres coordinator backends' free-text provenance column, the discovery/coordinator UI payload's job list, static/discovery_ui.js's rendering) already stores/echoes provenance as an unvalidated free string, so this was purely additive -- no schema or consumer change needed anywhere. utils/evidence_backend.py gained a sixth storage concern, ConsoleJobBackend (filesystem default + opt-in PostgreSQL, same abstraction shape as DEV.3.3's five), for durable job records under data_root/state/console_jobs, wired into verify_evidence_backend_ready()'s startup preflight. New console/registry.py (JOB_REGISTRY -- seven closed job types per C2-1, including cp_gaia_backup declared but refused per C2-6), console/jobs.py (ConsoleJobStore: C2-9 idempotency via a durable idempotency_key index, C2-5 crash recovery via sweep_orphaned_running(), forbidden fields excluded by construction -- JobRecord simply has no such field), console/runner.py (single-worker FIFO executor per C2-7; calls main.main() exactly as the scheduler's _evaluate_and_dispatch_due_workflows does and nothing else -- AC-2). console/app.py gained POST /api/jobs, GET /api/jobs, GET /api/jobs/{job_id}, GET /api/jobs/{job_id}/events (SSE, C2-10 -- job-record state transitions only, never collector output), GET /api/job-types; create_app()'s new job_store/runner parameters are optional (auto-constructed against an ephemeral in-memory coordinator when omitted) so CON.1's existing route-table test fixture and any read-only-only caller keep working unmodified. application/cli.py's --console branch now also calls services.build_collection_services() before run_console, so the console process holds one RuntimeCollectionServices for its whole lifetime -- passed to every job the runner executes, giving the same admission-state continuity across jobs that the scheduler already has across its own dispatch loop. static/console_actions.js gained the action surface in templates/console.html's Discovery module: job-type buttons (an operational-write type always renders BLOCKED per C2-6, never a button that would 409 on click), a recent-jobs table, and a manual SSE reader built on fetch()+ReadableStream rather than the native EventSource API, which cannot carry the Authorization bearer header CON.1's auth model requires.
builds.evidence: Full suite: 933 passed / 27 skipped / 2 failed (pytest_result.log), same two pre-existing order-pollution failures as the pre-build baseline (907/27/2), zero regressions; +26 from the new tests/test_con2_console_job_engine.py (AC-1..AC-11, plus C2-1/C2-3/C2-6 coverage -- every test patches main.main so no test contacts a device). tests/test_con1_operator_console_read_only.py's AC-2 route-table test updated in place to allow the one deliberate mutating route CON.2 adds (POST /api/jobs) -- every other route stays GET/HEAD only. Manual FastAPI TestClient walkthrough of the full job lifecycle (submit -> queued -> running -> succeeded, idempotent replay, all six AC-3 rejection cases, SSE stream to a terminal event) also run and observed directly during implementation. A real-Chromium interactive open (same monkeypatch-fixture technique CON.1's own real-browser close used, main.py --console against tests/fixtures/uitest): the new Discovery-module job panel rendered all six read-class job-type buttons plus cp_gaia_backup correctly dashed/disabled as 'Collect Check Point Gaia backup -- BLOCKED', clicking 'Rebuild report' drove a real console-triggered main.main(['--render-only']) run to completion with zero browser console errors -- confirmed not by the UI alone but by the scratch runtime root's output/index.html actually being rewritten on disk (1.45MB, freshly timestamped) -- and the jobs table updated to 'succeeded' with a run_id live via the SSE reader, no manual reload. Repository privacy gate PASS/0 (clean checkout; local run leaves the same known data//logs/ runtime artifacts every prior session's evidence also notes). Render harness unaffected (console_actions.js stays outside utils.html_export.MODULE_ORDER, asserted by test).
builds.risks_forward: Real-environment validation is owed before this phase advances past AUTOMATED_VALIDATED: a watched run on the corporate laptop where a read-class action triggered from the console reaches a real device and produces the artifact an equivalent CLI run would -- hardware-gated, not an engineering task, no new code needed. The provenance change (C2-3) was the widest-blast-radius item in this phase per the contract's own risk callout; the audit found it genuinely additive, but any future consumer that starts validating provenance against a fixed set (rather than storing it as free text) must add 'console' to that set. static/console_actions.js's SSE reader is hand-rolled (fetch()+ReadableStream, no native EventSource) specifically because EventSource cannot carry a bearer header under CON.1's cookieless auth model -- worth remembering if a later phase is tempted to switch back to EventSource for convenience. builds.title: D2 decision + RB.2 PAN device-state collection orchestration (IMPLEMENTED, real-env owed) + RB.4 validation (AUTOMATED_VALIDATED)
builds.summary: User directed: resolve D2, build RB.4, and build recovery collection under explicit constraints -- not inlined in main.py, selective per gateway, scheduler-integrated, mergeable with a future UI. D2 resolved 2026-08-30 (product owner approval, recorded in docs/design/BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY_ARCHITECTURE.md §13): PAN service account may hold superuser for device-state export only. New utils/recovery_collect.py is the single orchestration layer -- target selection (select_recovery_targets: 'all' or an explicit entity_id list including the VSX __vsid_ convention; an unresolvable id raises before any device is touched), a RecoveryCollector protocol for vendor dispatch, and run_recovery_collection routing every target through a caller-supplied admission hook so one gateway's failure never aborts the batch. panorama/panorama_recovery_collector.py implements PAN device-state export (contract §7.1, read class, gate-documented before this build) reusing panorama_runtime_runner.get_api_key/_tls_verify_setting verbatim with per-host API-key session reuse and no 403 retry. checkpoint/checkpoint_recovery_collector.py is a typed blocked stub (RecoveryCollectionBlockedError naming D3, unresolved -- CORRECTED during the main-merge on 2026-08-30: the P0 cp_device_interaction_safety audit itself closed 2026-08-25, before this build; D3 is the only real remaining blocker) so orchestration/store/admission wiring is already correct for CP once D3 is decided and the command gate signs off. utils/collection_executor.py: ALLOWLISTED_WORKFLOWS gains 'recovery-pan' (not 'recovery-cp'); ScheduledWorkflow gains an additive optional 'targets' field (schema version unchanged, every prior policy file's meaning preserved). main.py stays thin: --recovery-collect/--recovery-vendor/--recovery-gateways parse arguments and dispatch only; _scheduler_workflow_argv extended for recovery-pan. Separately, utils/recovery_validation.py (RB.4) implements the V1-V3 battery frozen in contract §4 and utils/recovery_store.revalidate_artifact wires it into the store (decrypt in memory only); main.py --recovery-validate gates on any individual check FAIL, not the top-line verdict alone, after a real bug was caught where a V2-only failure reported verdict=INTACT (V1 passed) and would have silently passed a naive gate.

evidence.automated: 85 new tests: tests/test_rb2_recovery_collect.py (25 -- target selection incl. VSX addressing and unresolvable-id request-time errors; run_recovery_collection integration writing a real encrypted artifact through the actual store, partial-batch-failure isolation, blocked-vs-failed outcome distinction, admission-hook call-per-target and rejection handling; CP stub always blocks with the exact reason string; PAN collector exercised only against a monkeypatched fixture HTTP transport -- 403-no-retry, session/key reuse across two collect() calls, missing-management_ip fails before any request; scheduler policy 'targets' field optional/additive and 'recovery-cp' rejected at load time; _scheduler_workflow_argv shape for both with and without targets; CLI integration through main.main() including the mandatory --recovery-vendor guard and a full blocked-CP run) and tests/test_rb4_recovery_validation.py (19 -- V1 hash/size PASS and FAIL-caps-at-V1; V2 gzip/XML well-formedness incl. the differentiator case of an artifact that is internally valid V1/V2 but claims the wrong device, correctly stuck at V2 not V3; V3 absent-inventory and version-mismatch NOT_APPLICABLE/FAIL semantics; restore_proven never settable without attach_restore_proof and its required-field/success-result checks; store-level revalidate_artifact round trip; CLI incl. the corrected any-check-FAIL gate). One pre-existing test updated in place, not routed around: tests/test_phase0_6_1c_collection_executor.py::test_allowlisted_workflows_are_read_only now asserts 'recovery-pan' present (read class) and 'recovery-cp' absent (write-adjacent, still gated) -- a genuine, intentional allowlist expansion, not a regression. py -m pytest -q: 741 passed, 3 skipped, 2 pre-existing unrelated failures unchanged from baseline. Repository privacy gate: PASS / 0.
evidence.manual_cli: Exercised end-to-end via main.main() and a real docker-compose-free --scheduler-once run against a throwaway runtime/recovery root with synthetic credentials and the uitest unified.json fixture: CP path (--recovery-collect --recovery-vendor checkpoint, both explicit-gateway and 'all' selector) fails closed immediately with the exact P0/D3 blocker text, gate FAIL, exit 1, zero artifacts written. PAN path resolves the target, acquires admission, attempts the real (unreachable-in-this-sandbox) HTTPS call, fails gracefully per-target with the real connection error surfaced, gate FAIL, exit 1 -- confirming the failure path degrades correctly rather than crashing. An unresolvable --recovery-gateways entry fails at argument-parse time (exit 2) before any device is contacted. A scheduler_policy.json entry for 'recovery-pan' with an explicit targets list was picked up correctly by --scheduler-once and dispatched through the identical --recovery-collect CLI path (verified by output), proving the CLI/scheduler code-sharing the product direction required actually holds, not just in unit tests.

builds.title: RB.1 recovery-plane store: encryption, manifest, retention, validator (no collection)
builds.summary: User request: implement RB.1 against the frozen docs/design/BACKUP_RECOVERY_CONTRACTS.md §2/§3/§8/§9. New utils/recovery_crypto.py (AES-256-GCM envelope encryption via the cryptography package, now pinned explicitly in requirements.txt instead of only a transitive paramiko dependency), utils/recovery_manifest.py (build_manifest/validate_manifest enforcing all five frozen §3 rules), utils/recovery_store.py (vault key resolution mirroring DEV.2.2's .support_hmac.key precedent -- the key lives on data_root, never on recovery_root -- plus write/read/decrypt-artifact and a consistency-group storage primitive), utils/recovery_retention.py (GFS plan_deletions as a pure function honoring the floor invariant, apply_deletions dry-run-by-default matching --storage-deduplicate's --apply convention). utils/runtime_paths.py gains resolve_recovery_root: SECURITYEXPERT_RECOVERY_ROOT, mandatory and absolute with deliberately NO OS-default (unlike runtime_root), validated separate from both the repository root and the runtime root via a generalized _validate_disjoint helper. main.py gains --recovery-store-check (offline diagnostic mirroring --persistent-secret-material-check) and --recovery-root. docker-compose.yml gains a securityexpert-recovery named volume mounted ONLY on worker, never nginx. utils/repository_privacy.py extended with the .enc suffix and a 'vault' forbidden root dir.

evidence.automated: 41 new tests in tests/test_rb1_recovery_store.py (new pytest.ini 'recovery' marker, shared with RB.0) covering every §9 security invariant assigned to RB.1: 9.1 (a real write_artifact call, then every file under recovery_root is grepped for an unmistakable plaintext marker -- none found, confirming ciphertext-only on disk including the atomic-write temp path), 9.2 (the vault-key resolver rejects a data_root nested under recovery_root), 9.4 (a real support bundle built via support_bundle.run_support_bundle alongside a populated recovery store contains none of its bytes, checked by unzipping and scanning every member), 9.5 (scan_repository flags a probe .enc file and a vault/ root dir), 9.6 (validate_manifest rejects a non-null restore block), 9.9 (a 200-iteration seeded-random property test over arbitrary fleets/policies: retention never reduces an entity below its configured floor, and never deletes the sole remaining is_rma_grade artifact even when it is nominally over the tier limit), 9.11 (docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.prod.yml parsed by indentation to isolate the nginx service's own lines, comments stripped, and asserted to never mention 'recovery'). Plus manifest-builder derivation rules (pan_running_config always is_rma_grade=false, pan_device_state/cp_gaia_backup always true, known_gaps auto-filled and rejected-if-empty for classes with documented vendor exclusions), crypto round-trips (encrypt/decrypt, wrap/unwrap) and two tamper-detection cases (wrong key, flipped ciphertext byte) both raising RecoveryCryptoError, vault-key persistence across a simulated restart (two independent get_or_create_vault_key calls against the same paths), and CLI integration through main.main() including the mandatory-env-var failure path. py -m pytest -q: 697 passed, 3 skipped, 2 pre-existing unrelated failures unchanged from baseline. Repository privacy gate: PASS / 0.
evidence.manual_cli: python main.py --recovery-store-check exercised directly against throwaway SECURITYEXPERT_RUNTIME_ROOT/SECURITYEXPERT_RECOVERY_ROOT: initializes vault/groups/retention under the recovery root, generates and persists the vault key at <data_root>/.recovery_vault.key (confirmed on disk, physically separate from the recovery root), prints only the key's opaque fingerprint (never the path or key bytes), reports zero artifacts held. The missing-SECURITYEXPERT_RECOVERY_ROOT and nested-inside-runtime-root cases both fail closed with actionable, value-free error messages (exit 2). docker compose config (base file and the docker-compose.prod.yml overlay) confirms the volume topology: worker mounts both securityexpert-runtime and securityexpert-recovery; nginx mounts only securityexpert-runtime.

builds.title: DEV.3.2 - Distributed per-endpoint lock and cross-process admission (Postgres)
builds.supersedes: distributed_endpoint_lock_and_job_store (split into this item + distributed_evidence_store_migration per the accepted contract)
builds.summary: User-approved contract implemented: CollectionCoordinator now delegates every admission decision to a CoordinatorBackend (utils/coordinator_backend.py); the default InMemoryCoordinatorBackend is the prior single-process logic moved verbatim (plus two incidental bug fixes: dead _endpoint_locks removed, budget_snapshot() undercounting above capacity 1 fixed). New opt-in PostgresCoordinatorBackend (SECURITYEXPERT_COORDINATOR_BACKEND=postgres) gives the per-endpoint exclusion and per-vendor budget a cross-process equivalent via session-level pg_advisory_lock held on a dedicated per-job connection (released by the server itself if the connection dies -- no TTL, no heartbeat), HMAC-derived lock keys so no device identity reaches Postgres, and a fail-closed startup preflight (verify_postgres_backend_ready) that detects a transaction-pooling proxy before use. main.py wires backend selection with a clean parser.error on failure and gates the scheduler read-evaluate-write cycle behind a scheduler-wide advisory lock on the Postgres backend. Concurrency budget value unchanged at 1; no collector/transport/command change.

evidence.automated: py -m pytest -q: 654 passed, 3 skipped, 2 failed (both pre-existing/unrelated, same two tests already documented against the unmodified baseline). Net +20 (tests/test_dev3_2_distributed_endpoint_lock.py), zero regressions.
evidence.real_postgres: Manually verified this session against a real local PostgreSQL 16 (not mocked): a real child OS process admitted first, an independent second backend instance coalesced onto it rather than opening a second session (AC-1); the child was SIGKILLed and reclamation happened with no TTL/heartbeat, the stale row marked orphaned (AC-3); a real pgbouncer 1.22 configured pool_mode=transaction was correctly rejected by the startup preflight (AC-5), while a direct connection passed it. main.py smoke-tested end-to-end (--scheduler-once) against the real Postgres backend and against an unreachable DSN (clean fail-closed error, not a traceback).
evidence.privacy_gate: No canonical_id, device name, address, credential or transport transcript is persisted to Postgres -- only HMAC-derived lock keys, job ids, vendor/scope labels, status and timestamps.
evidence.real_env: Real-environment validation against an actual multi-container deployment hitting a real Check Point MDS remains owed before DONE/REAL_ENV_VALIDATED -- server-blocked (DEPLOY.1, external).
